title: Accordion time-slicer for multi‑GPU token flow
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Problem: On heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters we see recurring tail latency spikes and suboptimal throughput when prefilling long contexts concurrently with decode-heavy workloads. The root causes are misaligned communication windows (NCCL), inefficient kernel selection for short vs long token windows, and contention between pipeline/tensor stages for NIC bandwidth.

Proposal (Accordion time-slicer): Implement an adaptive time-slicing scheduler that dynamically stretches and compresses per-stage prefill/decode windows (the 'accordion') to create predictable NCCL overlap opportunities while preserving steady-state decode throughput. Key ideas:
- Sliding window elasticity: measure stage latencies and available network bandwidth and adjust the duration of prefill vs decode micro-windows to maximize overlap without increasing peak memory.
- Kernel hinting API: expose a lightweight hint from the scheduler to the kernel-selection layer (e.g., prefer fused attention kernels for compressed windows, low-overhead tile kernels for stretched windows). Hints are best-effort and do not change model semantics.
- Attention tiling alignment: align attention-chunk boundaries across pipeline stages so NCCL collectives can coalesce into fewer, larger transfers when windows align, reducing overhead.
- KV prefetch steering: coordinate KV cache prefetches to happen just ahead of stretched windows to reduce blocking during short decode bursts.
- Backpressure and fairness: integrate a credit-based backpressure loop so large prefill requests cannot starve small low-latency decodes. The scheduler supports per-tenant QoS policies.

Goals: Reduce 95th/99th percentile end-to-end latency on mixed prefill+decode workloads; increase NCCL overlap fraction on measured traces; introduce minimal starve risk and be opt-in per deployment. Maintain compatibility with existing rollout and fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can be enabled behind a runtime flag (runtime.accordion.enabled=false by default)
End-to-end experiments on internal perf harness show >=10% reduction in 95th percentile latency for multi-GPU 4-8k context mixed workloads compared to baseline within the same infra profile
NCCL overlap fraction increases by >=15% in representative traces (measured with comm tracer)
Kernel hinting surface documented and accepted by kernel-selection owners; falls back safely when hint unsupported
No regression in stable unit tests and existing throughput SLOs (regression budget <2%)
Can be toggled via per-pool policy and respects per-tenant QoS labels
steps: Design: formalize accordion timing model and APIs between scheduler, router, and kernel selector
Sim: implement a lightweight event-driven simulator to tune window elasticity parameters using replay traces
Proto: implement scheduler + kernel hint pass in runtime (feature-flagged)
Bench: run microbenchmarks (prefill-only, decode-only, mixed) across a small fleet (4xA100, 8xA10) and collect NCCL/latency metrics
Iterate: adjust attention-tile alignment heuristics and KV prefetch offsets based on bench results
Rollout: canary in Dedicated pools -> observe -> expand to Hosted with per-tenant opt-in
Docs: publish operator guide, kernel-hint spec, and troubleshooting runbook
updates: 2025-02-14: Created. Initial problem statement and high-level approach. Collected representative traces from prod_dedicated_1 and dedicated_canary_3.

2025-02-16: Design review with kernel-selection and comm teams. Decided to expose a single byte-sized enum as the kernel hint (LOW_LATENCY, BALANCED, HIGH_THRU). Kernel team agreed to best-effort support.
2025-02-17: Simulator prototype implemented (python). Replay of 2000 mixed traces shows accordion reduces blocking windows by ~18% with default params.
2025-02-19: Spike PR created for scheduler plumbing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245. Initial integration tests pass on CI; one flaky test in pipeline reorder observed.

2025-02-20: Bench results from canary fleet (4xA100): 95p latency improved 11% on average; NCCL overlap increased by 12%. Trade-off: slight increase in memory jitter on extreme prefill bursts; mitigated by capping max stretch factor.

2025-02-21: Action items: (1) add credit-based backpressure to prevent tenant starvation, (2) harden kernel hint fallback path, (3) add observability charts for per-window NCCL fraction and hint adoption
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive stretching improves NCCL coalescing but can increase peak memory and risk starvation; we chose conservative defaults with per-pool caps.
We intentionally keep kernel hint semantics advisory to avoid coupling the scheduler to internal kernel invariants.
Related work: overlaps conceptually similar to token-wave strategies but focuses on elastic time windows rather than static microbatch reallocation.
Follow-ups: expose per-tenant QoS policies in Console and add cost telemetry for accordion-enabled pools
